# Millionærklubben Eksklusiv - del 2: Hvor meget kan markedet skælve uden helt at falde sammen?

**Feed**: millionaerklubben  
**Published**: 2026-11-26  
**Market Sentiment**: Mixed

⏱️ **Time Horizon Key**: ST = <3 months | MT = 3-12 months | LT = >12 months

---

## Episode Thesis

Part 2 of a Danish EuroInvestor Millionærklubben panel with Ulrik Bie, Thomas Thyssen and Sten Jacobsen on investing through a period of fast geopolitical and technological change. The panel agrees AI will change a lot, but doubts that today's expensive US AI and office-software leaders will capture the gains. They prefer industrial companies that build high technology into their products, defence, and Scandinavia/Northern Europe over the US and China. Sten also recommends broad ETFs, managed-futures (trend-following) ETFs such as DBMF, and investing in young founders, and says the market is still expensive and nervous.

---

## Universe Stocks

### 🟢 ABB — ABB | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Sten (guest) says industrial companies combining software with robots, like ABB, will be the big winners.

#### Reasoning

Sten's thesis: the next AI wave merges software with robotics, so under-valued industrial companies gain most. Also, the 10% of tangible assets must grow to supply the 90% intangible economy (power, infrastructure), helped by state-capitalist spending. Thomas agrees that industrials infused with AI are the long-term theme, with Scandinavia/Northern Europe preferred.

#### Sell Triggers

- if AI value accrues mainly to software or LLM providers rather than industrials
- if the industrial capex upcycle stalls
- if valuations already price in the robotics upside

> *"så får man en helt anden gevinst, så ABB i verden og nogle af de andre bliver de store vindere"*

---

### 🟢 INVE-B — Investor AB | **BUY** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 40%

Sten points to investment companies with stakes in many Swedish industrials as winners; Investor AB is implied, not named.

#### Reasoning

Sten argues the industrialised world wins from AI-enabled automation, and names investment companies owning parts of many Swedish industrials. Investor AB fits this but was not named outright. Thomas adds that Nordic high-tech industrials with stable macro are the place to be.

#### Sell Triggers

- if Swedish industrial holdings underperform the AI/automation shift
- if the Nordic macro advantage erodes

> *"De store industriselskaber og investere osv., som ejer en lille del af en masse, eller en stor del af mange svenske selskaber."*

---

### 🟠 SAAB-B — Saab | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 50%

Thomas cites Saab's AI-piloted fighter jet test as the kind of high-tech defence that is the future.

#### Reasoning

Thomas's long-term themes for 2027 and beyond are European industry and defence with built-in high technology, now that AI is cheap enough to build robots. Saab's AI-pilot test is his example. He warns US-related news may drown out this theme in the short term.

#### Sell Triggers

- if US market turmoil drowns out the European defence/industry theme
- if European defence spending commitments weaken

> *"Jeg så lige her forleden dag, at Saab havde prøvefløjet igen. deres jægerfly med AI-pilot. Det er efter min mening den slags ting, der er fremtiden."*

---

### 🟢 DBMF — DBMF | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 70%

Sten recommends the DBMF managed-futures ETF as a portfolio counterweight; about +20% YTD vs a flat equity market.

#### Reasoning

Sten (guest) uses managed futures/trend-following when parking money. They tend to move against the market, which balances a portfolio. DBMF copies trend-follower positions, is up about 20% this year, and he says it has worked reasonably well. Thomas warns clients may lose patience when diversifiers lag.

#### Sell Triggers

- if trend-following strategies stop being negatively correlated with equities
- if prolonged underperformance during equity rallies

> *"der er en, der hedder DB, ligesom Deutsche Bank, MF, den er ikke lavet af Deutsche Bank, men den hedder DB MF, som er en ETF, som laver en kopi af alle positioner, som de her trendfollower har."*

---

### 🟠 GOOGL — Google | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Mixed | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 40%

Sten expects Google to win in enterprise AI but seems to say he would not buy it now. The wording is unclear.

#### Reasoning

Sten argues AI winners are those who own the customers. Google has the full product range, enterprise customers and a business model where the products are free to use. However, he warns that it is too early to pick winners (like carmakers in 1900) and prefers broad ETFs, so this is a watch, not a buy.

#### Sell Triggers

- if Google loses enterprise customer share
- if AI becomes commoditised and free, crushing monetisation

> *"det obvious er, at som jeg ikke vil købe Google her, så Google kommer til at vinde på Enterprise-siden"*

---

### ⛔ NVDA — Nvidia | **AVOID** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Negative | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 50%

Sten says Nvidia is already priced to perfection; the panel doubts the early AI leaders will make the money.

#### Reasoning

Sten contrasts early-stage 5x-100x opportunities with buying Nvidia at a priced-to-perfection valuation. Both he and Thomas think early AI leaders, like 1999 broadband, will not be the ones that profit, and that AI will become very cheap. Ulrik notes pension funds hold it only to track benchmarks.

#### Sell Triggers

- if AI demand monetisation exceeds expectations
- if valuation resets to attractive levels

> *"i stedet for at du køber en Navidia, som allerede er prisfast til perfektion"*
